operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 636-2335 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10371.txt, 17 FR 6213): signed 1952-07-09; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, TWA Chapter; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order and directs the board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 101; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10371_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10371_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_bd80a51a81.txt) bears the cover date AUGUST 29, 1952 (date line at offsets 1151-1166 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1952-08-29. The report states that, before the hearings closed, the parties agreed to an extension of the original time limit to September 7 and that the President approved the extension (report text offsets 6067-6300); it also bears a transmittal letter dated in August 1952 whose date line is OCR-damaged. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1952-09-28 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10371 appears in the table at offset 10118 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt together with the subject line for an airline labor dispute board. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10371
Creating an E mergency  B oard T o I nves ­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  the  T rans
W orld A irlines , I nc., and C ertain  op
I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Plight Engineers’  International 
Association, TWA Chapter, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
T J . S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Trans World Airlines, Inc., 
or its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.
In performing its functions under this 
order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
EO 10371 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline , a Defense Production Act section 502 compliance direction and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1952-08-29 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 1542-3224 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10406.txt, 17 FR 10131): signed 1952-11-06; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the United Air Lines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, UAL Chapter; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order and directs the board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 103; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10406_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10406_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_0afc851ff8.txt) bears the cover date JANUARY 2,1953 (date line at offsets 1147-1161 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1953-01-02. The report states that, before the hearings closed, the parties agreed to a 30-day extension of the time limit stated in the Executive order and that on December 1, 1952 the President approved it (report text offsets 4991-5200); its letter of transmittal is also dated January 2, 1953. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1953-02-01 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10406 appears in the table at offset 10384 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10406
Creating an E mergency B oard T o I n ­
vestigate a D ispute  B etween  the 
United A ir Lines , I nc., and C ertain of 
Its E mployees  >
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the United Air Lines, Inc., a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the Flight Engineers’  International As­
sociation, UAL Chapter, a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt 
interstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the United Air Lines, Inc., or its 
employees in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.
In performing its functions under this 
order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments (option B), the amendment is a clause that continues, as amended, until the parent order ends; the parent EO 9949 is itself named in the EO 12553 table (offset 5212 of the held EO 12553 text), as is EO 9721 (offset 1105). The December 31, 1953 date limits the time within which the employee's service had to end to qualify; it is a condition deadline written into the clause, not an end of the order, and is treated as functionally spent on 1953-12-31 by analogy to the report-deadline ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C). Alternative reading, disclosed for the reviewer: the clause could be read to lapse by its own terms after 1953-12-31 because the modified condition could no longer be met by a later termination; the held evidence does not show whether the employee's service ended before that date or whether any reemployment right accrued, so no earlier end is established. Earlier candidate end under the unnamed-instruments ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C): Executive Order 10804, signed 1959-02-12 (held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10804.txt, section 2 at offsets 1193-2145), revoked Executive Order 9721 and Executive Order 10103 except for employees then serving with an international organization and for rights vested before the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act; it does not name EO 9949 or EO 10415, so it is not treated as their end. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10415 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10390 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). research_rationale:
EO 10511 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1954-05-15 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10511 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. The revocation in EO 12553 has no exception text, so it reaches the whole order."}

The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 607-2099 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10542.txt, 19 FR 4117): signed 1954-07-06; creates under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 a Board of Inquiry of members to be appointed by the President to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between Union Carbide and Carbon Corporation and certain of its employees represented by Locals 288 and 550, United Gas, Coke, and Chemical Workers, CIO, at Atomic Energy Commission facilities at Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and Paducah, Kentucky; gives the Board the powers and duties set out in Title II of that Act; directs it to report in accordance with section 206 on or before July 20, 1954; and provides that after the report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as the Act requires until the President terminates it. The July 20, 1954 date is a report deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C, applied to this board-of-inquiry order by analogy; the order's own end is the Presidential termination, which is a contingent event). No instrument terminating the Board, and no board report, is held in the packet or located by the number-citation scan of held texts, so neither a report date nor a Presidential termination is established, and a termination by a Presidential act that is not a held instrument is not excluded; the order is not treated as ended by performance. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10542 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10452 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain contains only EO 12553 where an acting provision is located, and the number-citation scan lists no other later order naming this order.

WHEREAS there exists a labor dis­
pute between the Union Carbide and 
Carbon Corporation and certain of its 
employees represented by Locals 288 and 
550, United Gas, Coke, and Chemical 
Workers, CIO, at certain facilities of the 
Atomic Energy Commission located in 
Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and Paducah, 
Kentucky; and
WHEREAS in my opinion such dispute 
threatens to result in a strike affecting 
a substantial part of an industry en­
gaged in trade or commerce among the 
several States or with foreign nations, or 
in the production of goods for com­
merce, which strike, if permitted to occur 
or to continue, will imperil the national 
safety; -  '¿ x fll

form such other functions as may be

research_rationale:
EO 10542 creates a Taft-Hartley section 206 Board of Inquiry for an Atomic Energy Commission contractor dispute. Its commands are creation of the board, a report deadline and continuation until the President terminates the board. The report deadline is not an end; no Presidential termination instrument is held; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The caveat that a non-held Presidential act could have terminated the board earlier is stated in the clause reason and is not filled by inference. Searches: no U.S. Code or eCFR hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search adds nothing beyond EO 12553 in the dossier chain.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 2211-3728 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10543.txt, 19 FR 4117): signed 1954-07-06; creates under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 a Board of Inquiry of members to be appointed by the President to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between Union Carbide and Carbon Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Atomic Trades and Labor Council, AFL, and associated local unions, at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the Y-12 area facilities, Oak Ridge, Tennessee; gives the Board the powers and duties set out in Title II of that Act; directs it to report in accordance with section 206 on or before July 20, 1954; and provides that after the report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as the Act requires until the President terminates it. The July 20, 1954 date is a report deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C, applied to this board-of-inquiry order by analogy; the order's own end is the Presidential termination, which is a contingent event). No instrument terminating the Board, and no board report, is held in the packet or located by the number-citation scan of held texts, so neither a report date nor a Presidential termination is established, and a termination by a Presidential act that is not a held instrument is not excluded; the order is not treated as ended by performance. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10543 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10458 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain contains only EO 12553 where an acting provision is located, and the number-citation scan lists no other later order naming this order.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10543
Creating a B oard of I nquiry  T o R eport 
on a L abor D ispute  A ffecting  the 
Operations  of A tomic E nergy F acil­
ities
WHEREAS there exists a labor dis­
pute between the Union Carbide and 
Carbon Corporation and certain of its 
employees represented by the Atomic 
Trades and Labor Council, AFL, and the 
local unions associated with the Council, 
at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory 
and the facilities located in the Y-12 
area, Oak Ridge, Tennessee; and 
WHEREAS in my opinion such dis­
pute threatens to result in a strike af­
fecting a substantial part of an industry 
engaged in trade or commerce among 
the seyeral States Or with foreign na­
tions, or in the production of goods for 
commerce, which strike, if permitted to 
occur or to continue, will imperil the na­
tional health and safety:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 206 of 
the Labor-Management Relations Act, 
1947, 61 Stat. 155, I hereby create a 
Board of Inquiry, consisting of such 
members as I shall appoint, to inquire 
into the issues involved in such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and 
duties as set forth in Title II of the said 
Act. The Board shall report to the 
President in accordance with the provi­
sions of section 206 of the said Act on or 
before July 20, 1954.
Upon submission of its report, the 
Board shall continue in existence to per­
form such other functions as may be 
required under the said Act, until the 
Board is terminated by the President.

research_rationale:
EO 10543 creates a Taft-Hartley section 206 Board of Inquiry for an Atomic Energy Commission contractor dispute. Its commands are creation of the board, a report deadline and continuation until the President terminates the board. The report deadline is not an end; no Presidential termination instrument is held; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The caveat that a non-held Presidential act could have terminated the board earlier is stated in the clause reason and is not filled by inference. Searches: no U.S. Code or eCFR hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search adds nothing beyond EO 12553 in the dossier chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the report deadline is a deadline and not an end; (2) the continuation until Presidential termination is a contingent end whose event is not shown by any held instrument or report; (3) no order other than EO 12553 revokes, amends or supersedes this order in the dossier chain or the number-citation scan; (4) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The powers, duties and further functions of the Board are those set out in Title II of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, so they arise under the statute; the statute is not held in the packet and its text was not analyzed here. The order itself creates no continuing right, appropriation or office apart from the Board.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms), so it reaches the whole order. No accrued right or later-effective duty arising only from the order is shown by held evidence; the Board and its statutory proceedings were a mid-1950s dispute procedure.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, exception or delayed effective date, and EO 12553 contains no exception text."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 621-2076 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10570.txt, 19 FR 6687): signed 1954-10-16; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Pullman Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 107; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10570_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10570_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_f1cbeae2b3.txt) bears the cover date NOVEMBER 20, 1954 (date line at offsets 1190-1207 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1954-11-20. The report states that by stipulation of the parties the time for making the report was extended to November 26, 1954 (report text offsets 2848-2990); its letter of transmittal is also dated November 20, 1954. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1954-12-20 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10570 appears in the table at offset 10470 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10570
Creating an Emergency Board to Inves­
tigate a Dispute Between the Pull­
man Company and Certain op Its
Employees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between
The Pullman Company, a carrier, and
certain of its employees represented by
the Order of Railway Conductors and
Brakemen, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as
to deprive a section of the country of
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the
authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of
three members, to be appointed by me,
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to
the President with respect to the said
dispute within thirty days from the date
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this
date and for thirty days after the board
has made its report to the President, no
change, except by agreement, shall be
made by The Pullman Company, or by
its employees, in the conditions out of
which the said dispute arose.

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the 
United States Code which are quoted in the subsections of this section 
shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

ecutive Order No. 10119 of March 27,

ized by section 301 of the Career Com­

hereafter amended.”

EO 10605 is a strike-and-insert or addition amendment of a pay-and-allowance regulation order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option B) its clauses continue, as amended, until the parent order ends. The first held end is the express revocation by EO 11157 section 502 (signed 1964-06-22, no effective-date wording), which names this order and its parent. The 1962 title 37 recodification is disclosed as an unnamed earlier candidate that I read as restating without substantive change (Public Law 87-649 section 12). Searches: no U.S. Code or eCFR hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists the chain events recorded in the dossier.

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the 
United States Code which are quoted in the subsections of this section 
shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

S ec. 401. As used in this p a rt:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall apply to a mem­
ber while on the active list or while required to perform duty in accord­
ance with law for which he is entitled to basic pay: Provided , That such 
term shall not apply to any member while absent from duty under 
conditions which, under laws governing the particular service con­
cerned, would prevent him from receiving full Dasic pay.
(b) The term “field duty” shall mean service by a member under 
orders with troops operating against an enemy, actual or potential, or 
service with troops on maneuvers, war games, field exercises, or similar 
types of operations.
(c) The term “sea duty” shall mean service performed by either 
officer or enlisted members under conditions for which “sea duty” pay 
is payable to enlisted members in accordance with section 305 of title 
37 of the United States Code, and regulations issued thereunder.
(d) The term “permanent station” shall mean the place on shore 
where a member is assigned to duty, or the home yard or the home port 
of a ship in which a member is required to perform duty, under orders 
in each case which do not in terms provide for the termination thereof; 
and any station on shore or any receiving ship where a member is as­
signed and in fact occupies, with his dependents, if any, quarters under
- the jurisdiction of any of the uniformed services shall also be deemed 
during such occupancy to be his permanent station: Provided , That in 
the case of members of the National Guard, the Air National Guard 
or reserve components of any of the uniformed services on active duty 
for training, the place where the training duty is being qierformed 
shall be deemed to be the permanent station of such members for the 
purposes of these regulations.
S ec. 402. Except as otherwise by statute heretofore or hereafter 
provided, a member shall be entitled to payment of basic allowances 
for quarters, in accordance with these regulations and any regulations 
prescribed pursuant hereto, during shell time or times as he is entitled 
to receive basic pay.
S ec. 403. Any quarters or housing facilities under the jurisdiction 
of any of the uniformed services in fact occupied without payment of 
rental charges (a) by a member and his dependents, or (b) at his 
permanent station by a member without dependents, or (c) by the 
dependents of a member on field duty or on sea duty or on duty at a 
station where adequate quarters are not available for his dependents, 
shall be deemed to have been assigned to such member as appropriate 
and adequate quarters, and no basic allowance for quarters shall 
accrue to such member under such circumstances unless the occupancy
(i) occurs while such member is in a duty or leave status incident to 
a change of/ permanent station and is of a temporary nature under 
standards prescribed by regulations issued by the Secretary of Defense 
in the case of members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine 
Corps, and the reserve components thereof, or by the appropriate 
Secretary in the case of members of the other uniformed services, or
(ii) occurs while such member is in a leave status not incident to a 
change of permanent station and does not exceed seven consecutive 
days at one location: Provided , That occupancy of quarters under such 
circumstances for a period in excess of such 7-day period or such other 
temporary period as may be authorized under standards prescribed 
by regulations issued by the Secretary concerned shall not result in 
a forfeiture of basic allowance for quarters for such 7-day or other 
authorized period: Provided further , That this paragraph shall not 
apply to occupancy of quarters as a guest of another member.
S ec. 404. When adequate quarters for his dependents are not avail­
able for assignment at his perfnanent station to a member with de­
pendents, he may occupy quarters of the United States designated for 
members without dependents without affecting his right to receive 
payment of basic allowances for quarters, if permitted or required to 
occupy quarters at such station. Under such circumstances, a member 
may not occupy quarters of the United States which exceed the mini­
mum standards for members of his grade without dependents, as

able (a) exceed the minimum standards, and (b) are made available 
for joint occupancy with other members.

quarters of the United States designated for members without de­
pendents at his temporary duty station without affecting his right to 
receive payment of basic allowances for quarters or assignment of 
quarters, if any, at his permanent station. Under such circumstances, 
a member may not occupy quarters of the United States which exceed

as prescribed by the Secretary concerned, unless the only quarters

able for joint occupancy with other members.

or possessions in a duty assignment which has official or diplomatic 
responsibilities involving officials of foreign governments may be 
assigned quarters in excess of the minimum standards set forth in

tion 101(5) of title 37 of the United States Code), with respect to per­
sonnel of the uniformed services within their respective departments,

shall be uniform for all the services to the fullest extent practicable.

missioned officer without dependents who is in a pay grade above pay 
grade 0 -3  and who is assigned to quarters of the United States or a 
housing facility under the jurisdiction of a uniformed service, appro­
priate to his grade or rank and adequate for himself, may elect not to 
occupy those quarters and instead to receive the basic allowance for 
quarters prescribed for his pay grade by section 403 of title 37 of the. 
United States Code.

S ec. 501. For the purposes of these regulations, the terms defined 
in sections 101 and 401 of title 37 of the United States Code shall have 
the meanings prescribed therein.

(d) Executive Order No. 10204 of January 15,1951.
(e) Executive Order No. 10605 of April 22,1955.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 644-2388 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10615.txt, 20 FR 4315): signed 1955-06-17; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between certain carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (list A attached to the order) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. The attached list or lists identify the carriers and organizations that are parties; they are part of the order but state no separate command. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). No board report for this order is held in the packet (the number-citation scan of held texts finds only the order's own Federal Register page), so the actual report date and the end of the standstill are not recorded; they are spent facts that would not change the end below. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10615 appears in the table at offset 10514 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10615
Creating an  E mergency  B oard T o I n ­
vestigate a D ispute  B etw een C ertain  
Carriers R epresented  b y the  E astern , 
W estern , and S outheastern  C arriers ’ 
Conference  C ommittees  and C ertain  
of T heir  E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the East­
ern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers’ 
Conference Committees which are desig­
nated in List A attached hereto and 
made a part hereof, and certain of their 
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Locomotive Firemen and Engine- 
men, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in  the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of employees or any 
carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
their employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 1616-3177 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10630.txt, 20 FR 5911): signed 1955-08-13; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the New York Central System, Lines East, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 112; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10630_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10630_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_814b8eb677.txt) bears the cover date SEPTEMBER 14, 1955 (date line at offsets 1176-1194 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1955-09-14. The held front-matter excerpt of the report records no extension of the time limit; its letter of transmittal bears the same city and a September date whose day is OCR-damaged. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1955-10-14 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10630 appears in the table at offset 10528 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10630
Creating an E mergency  B oard T o I n ­
vestigate a D ispute  B etw een the  N ew  
York Central S ystem , Lines  E ast, and 
Certain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the New York Central System, Lines 
East, a carrier, and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the Order of Rail­
way Conductors and Brakemen, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said Board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, 
no change, except by agreement, shall 
be made by the New York Central Sys­
tem, Lines East, or by its employees, in 
the conditions out of which the said 
dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 889-1833 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10634.txt, 20 FR 6433): signed 1955-08-25; under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, provides that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations and guarantees) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, when the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. No own-terms sunset or condition ends the order. Later orders EO 10773 (1958; list entry 14), EO 11051 (1962; section 601 list) and EO 11725 (1973; list entry 7) mention EO 10634 in enumerated lists of orders in orders that redirect references to, or authority of, successor mobilization and emergency-preparedness offices; they are later events about which office exercises the determination, and I found no language in them that revokes or terminates EO 10634 (the dossier lists their acting provisions as not located; I read the list entries in the held texts jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-10773-delegating-and-transferring-certain-functions-and-affairs-the-office.txt, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11051.txt and jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11725.txt, but did not read each of those orders end to end). First end: Executive Order 12148, Federal Emergency Management, section 5-106, which states that Executive Order 10634, as amended, relating to loans for facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, is revoked; its closing section states that the order is effective July 15, 1979 (offsets 23765-23802 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12148.txt; the revocation sentence is at offsets 16364-16497). EO 12148 was signed 1979-07-20, so the effective date is retroactive by its own words; the first end is recorded on the stated effective date, 1979-07-15, with the signing date disclosed. No held source shows an earlier lapse of the Defense Production Act section 302 authority that the order invokes; that possibility is not excluded but is not supported by held evidence, and the order is permissive, so it is not treated as ended by disuse.

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the

shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would

(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­

pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

research_rationale:
EO 10681 is a strike-and-insert or addition amendment of a pay-and-allowance regulation order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option B) its clauses continue, as amended, until the parent order ends. The first held end is the express revocation by EO 11157 section 502 (signed 1964-06-22, no effective-date wording), which names this order and its parent. The 1962 title 37 recodification is disclosed as an unnamed earlier candidate that I read as restating without substantive change (Public Law 87-649 section 12). Searches: no U.S. Code or eCFR hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists the chain events recorded in the dossier.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the clauses have no sunset or condition of their own; (2) later amendments of the parent order (EO 11120 and, for EO 10681 and EO 10739, EO 10739 and EO 10618) amend other sections and do not replace the clause text; (3) Public Law 87-649 (1962 recodification) does not name this order and, by its section 12, restates the replaced law without substantive change and carries references and actions forward, so it is a disclosed candidate and not an end; (4) EO 11157 section 502 names EO 10681 and its parent orders and is the first instrument held that ends the clauses.","independent_command_check":"The pay and allowance entitlements themselves arise under the statutes (the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and, after its recodification, title 37 of the United States Code), which are not held in the packet as evidence records; the order only prescribes the regulation text. EO 11157 independently prescribes the corresponding rule after 1964-06-22.","savings_check":"EO 11157 contains no savings wording (the held text was searched for accrued, prior to, savings, nothing in and shall not affect). The substantive rule was carried forward by EO 11157 itself (section 104(c) at offsets 6050-6500 of the held EO 11157 text restates the mixed active-duty and inactive-duty flight requirement), so the rule is transferred to the replacing order; Public Law 87-649 section 14 preserves rights that matured before its effective date, which I note but do not rely on.","scope_check":"All scopes are parts of one amendment and end on the same date; EO 11157 section 502 has no exception text and revokes the order as a whole."}

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the 
United States Code which are quoted in the subsections of this section 
shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

S ec. 401. As used in this p a rt:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall apply to a mem­
ber while on the active list or while required to perform duty in accord­
ance with law for which he is entitled to basic pay: Provided , That such 
term shall not apply to any member while absent from duty under 
conditions which, under laws governing the particular service con­

orders with troops operating against an enemy, actual or potential, or 
service with troops on maneuvers, war games, field exercises, or similar 
types of operations.

officer or enlisted members under conditions for which “sea duty” pay 
is payable to enlisted members in accordance with section 305 of title 
37 of the United States Code, and regulations issued thereunder.
(d) The term “permanent station” shall mean the place on shore 
where a member is assigned to duty, or the home yard or the home port 
of a ship in which a member is required to perform duty, under orders 
in each case which do not in terms provide for the termination thereof; 
and any station on shore or any receiving ship where a member is as­
signed and in fact occupies, with his dependents, if any, quarters under
- the jurisdiction of any of the uniformed services shall also be deemed 
during such occupancy to be his permanent station: Provided , That in 
the case of members of the National Guard, the Air National Guard 
or reserve components of any of the uniformed services on active duty 
for training, the place where the training duty is being qierformed 
shall be deemed to be the permanent station of such members for the 
purposes of these regulations.
S ec. 402. Except as otherwise by statute heretofore or hereafter 
provided, a member shall be entitled to payment of basic allowances 
for quarters, in accordance with these regulations and any regulations 
prescribed pursuant hereto, during shell time or times as he is entitled 
to receive basic pay.
S ec. 403. Any quarters or housing facilities under the jurisdiction 
of any of the uniformed services in fact occupied without payment of 
rental charges (a) by a member and his dependents, or (b) at his 
permanent station by a member without dependents, or (c) by the 
dependents of a member on field duty or on sea duty or on duty at a 
station where adequate quarters are not available for his dependents, 
shall be deemed to have been assigned to such member as appropriate 
and adequate quarters, and no basic allowance for quarters shall 
accrue to such member under such circumstances unless the occupancy
(i) occurs while such member is in a duty or leave status incident to 
a change of/ permanent station and is of a temporary nature under 
standards prescribed by regulations issued by the Secretary of Defense 
in the case of members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine 
Corps, and the reserve components thereof, or by the appropriate 
Secretary in the case of members of the other uniformed services, or
(ii) occurs while such member is in a leave status not incident to a 
change of permanent station and does not exceed seven consecutive 
days at one location: Provided , That occupancy of quarters under such 
circumstances for a period in excess of such 7-day period or such other 
temporary period as may be authorized under standards prescribed 
by regulations issued by the Secretary concerned shall not result in 
a forfeiture of basic allowance for quarters for such 7-day or other 
authorized period: Provided further , That this paragraph shall not 
apply to occupancy of quarters as a guest of another member.
S ec. 404. When adequate quarters for his dependents are not avail­
able for assignment at his perfnanent station to a member with de­
pendents, he may occupy quarters of the United States designated for 
members without dependents without affecting his right to receive 
payment of basic allowances for quarters, if permitted or required to 
occupy quarters at such station. Under such circumstances, a member 
may not occupy quarters of the United States which exceed the mini­
mum standards for members of his grade without dependents, as

prescribed by the Secretary concerned, unless the only quarters avail­
able (a) exceed the minimum standards, and (b) are made available 
for joint occupancy with other members.
S ec. 405. A member away from his permanent station may occupy 
quarters of the United States designated for members without de­
pendents at his temporary duty station without affecting his right to 
receive payment of basic allowances for quarters or assignment of 
quarters, if any, at his permanent station. Under such circumstances, 
a member may not occupy quarters of the United States which exceed 
the minimum standards for members of his grade without dependents, 
as prescribed by the Secretary concerned, unless the only quarters 
available (a) exceed the minimum standards, and (b) are made avail­
able for joint occupancy with other members.
S ec. 406. A member serving outside the United States, its territories, 
or possessions in a duty assignment which has official or diplomatic 
responsibilities involving officials of foreign governments may be 
assigned quarters in excess of the minimum standards set forth in 
sections 404 and 405 hereof, as prescribed by the Secretary concerned: 
Provided , That no such quarters shall be available on a continuous 
basis for single occupancy, if such quarters are otherwise adequate for 
assignment as family housing to members of similar rank.
S ec. 407. The Secretaries concerned (within the meaning of sec­
tion 101(5) of title 37 of the United States Code), with respect to per­
sonnel of the uniformed services within their respective departments, 
are hereby authorized to prescribe such supplementary regulations not 
inconsistent herewith as they may deem necessary or desirable for 
carrying out these regulations, and such supplementary regulations 
shall be uniform for all the services to the fullest extent practicable.
S ec. 408. Unless the Secretary concerned, /or his designee, deter­
mines that military operational conditions require otherwise, a com­
missioned officer without dependents who is in a pay grade above pay 
grade 0 -3  and who is assigned to quarters of the United States or a 
housing facility under the jurisdiction of a uniformed service, appro­
priate to his grade or rank and adequate for himself, may elect not to 
occupy those quarters and instead to receive the basic allowance for 
quarters prescribed for his pay grade by section 403 of title 37 of the. 
United States Code.
P art Y — General  P rovisions
S ec. 501. For the purposes of these regulations, the terms defined 
in sections 101 and 401 of title 37 of the United States Code shall have 
the meanings prescribed therein.

(c) Executive Order No. 10168 of October 11,1950.
(d) Executive Order No. 10204 of January 15,1951.
(e) Executive Order No. 10605 of April 22,1955.
( f ) Executive Order No. 10618 of June 28,1955.
(g) Executive Order No. 10681 of October 22,1956.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 625-2268 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10691.txt, 21 FR 9735): signed 1956-12-05; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Spokane, Portland and Seattle Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). No board report for this order is held in the packet (the number-citation scan of held texts finds only the order's own Federal Register page), so the actual report date and the end of the standstill are not recorded; they are spent facts that would not change the end below. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10691 appears in the table at offset 10577 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10691
Creating an E mergency  B oard to I n­
vestigate a D ispute  B etween  the 
Spokane , Portland & Seattle Railway  
Company  and C ertain of I ts E m­
ployees  Represented by the B rother­
hood of L ocomotive Engineers
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Spokane, Portland and Seattle Rail­
way Company, a carrier, and certain of 
its employees represented by the Broth­
erhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the Country of es­
sential transportation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by Section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said Board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of railway employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Spokane, Portland and 
Seattle Railway Company, or by its em­
ployees, in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 10691 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). No board report is held; no spent-fact later event is recorded. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10691 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 1957-3801 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10693.txt, 21 FR 10325): signed 1956-12-22; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (list attached to the order) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. The attached list or lists identify the carriers and organizations that are parties; they are part of the order but state no separate command. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). No board report for this order is held in the packet (the number-citation scan of held texts finds only the order's own Federal Register page), so the actual report date and the end of the standstill are not recorded; they are spent facts that would not change the end below. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10693 appears in the table at offset 10583 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

EO 10693 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). No board report is held; no spent-fact later event is recorded. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 613-2136 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10710.txt, 22 FR 3405): signed 1957-05-14; creates under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 a Board of Inquiry of members to be appointed by the President to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between Goodyear Atomic Corporation and certain of its employees represented by Local 10-689, Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers International Union, AFL-CIO, at the Portsmouth Plant of the Atomic Energy Commission near Waverly, Ohio (the order recites that the dispute has resulted in a strike); gives the Board the powers and duties set out in Title II of that Act; directs it to report in accordance with section 206 on or before May 15, 1957; and provides that after the report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as the Act requires until the President terminates it. The May 15, 1957 date is a report deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C, applied to this board-of-inquiry order by analogy; the order's own end is the Presidential termination, which is a contingent event). No instrument terminating the Board, and no board report, is held in the packet or located by the number-citation scan of held texts, so neither a report date nor a Presidential termination is established, and a termination by a Presidential act that is not a held instrument is not excluded; the order is not treated as ended by performance. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10710 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10601 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain contains only EO 12553 where an acting provision is located, and the number-citation scan lists no other later order naming this order.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10710
Creating a B oard  o p I n q u ir y T o R eport  
on a L abor D is p u t e A ffe c tin g th e 
Operations  of  A to m ic E n e r g y F a c il i­
