WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute  
between the Goodyear Atomic Corpora­
tion and certain of its employees repre­
sented by Local 10-689, Oil, Chemical,  
and Atomic Workers International  
Union, AFL-CIO, at certain facilities  
(known as the Portsmouth Plant) of the  
Atomic, Energy Commission located near 
Waverly, Ohio; and
WHEREAS such dispute has resulted  
in a strike which, in my opinion, affects  
a substantial part of an industry en­
gaged in trade or commerce among the  
several States or with foreign nations, or 
in the production of goods for commerce, 
which strike, if permitted to continue,  
will imperil the national safety:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 206 of 
the Labor-Management Relations Act,  
1 9 4 7 , 61 Stat. 155, I hereby create a 
Board of Inquiry, consisting of such  
members as I shall appoint, to inquire  
into the issues involved in such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and du­
ties as set forth in Title n  of the said  
Act. The Board shall report to the  
President in accordance with the pro­
visions of section 206 of the said Act on  
or before May 15,1957. .
Upon submission of its report, the  
Board shall continue in existence to  
Perform such other functions as may be  
required under the said Act, until the  
Board is terminated by the President.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 623-3583 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10723.txt, 22 FR 6319): signed 1957-08-06; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the General Managers' Association of New York, representing twelve named railroads, and certain of their employees represented by the International Organization of Masters, Mates and Pilots, Inc.; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). No board report for this order is held in the packet (the number-citation scan of held texts finds only the order's own Federal Register page), so the actual report date and the end of the standstill are not recorded; they are spent facts that would not change the end below. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10723 appears in the table at offset 10613 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

research_rationale:
EO 10723 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). No board report is held; no spent-fact later event is recorded. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.

The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 708-1702 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10738.txt, 22 FR 9205): signed 1957-11-15; orders that any estate or gift tax return made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 or the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 be open to inspection by any official, body or commission lawfully charged with the administration of any State tax law, in accordance with the Treasury regulations and decision it names, and states that the order is effective upon its filing for publication in the Federal Register. Later partial events, recorded as later events and not as the end: (1) Executive Order 10906, signed 1961-01-17 and filed 1961-01-18 (F.R. Doc. 61-564, filing line at offset 3374 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10906.txt; its paragraph on effectiveness is at offsets 2872-3350), became effective on filing and on that date superseded EO 10738 to the extent applicable to inspection by State tax officials, after the effective date, of estate and gift-tax returns made under the 1939 or 1954 Code; (2) Executive Order 10954, signed 1961-07-26, replaced that paragraph with a version limited to returns made under the 1954 Code and provided that it is effective as of 1961-01-18. After EO 10954 the supersession reaches only 1954-Code returns, so the command continued for estate and gift tax returns made under the 1939 Code (the amendment is retroactive to the same day, so the net effect from 1961-01-18 is a supersession limited to 1954-Code returns). The clause therefore continued in part after 1961 and ended as a whole only when revoked. A possible earlier statutory extinguishment through later rewriting of Internal Revenue Code section 6103 is not shown by any held source and is not relied on. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10738 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10632 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. EO 12553 has no exception text, so the revocation reaches the remaining 1939-Code portion.

ERAL GOVERNMENT ESTABLISH­
MENTS OF RETURNS MADE IN RE­
SPECT OF CERTAIN TAXES IMPOSED  
BY THE INTERNAL REVENUE CODE  
OF 1954
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by sections 6103(a) and 6106 of the In ­
ternal Revenue Code of 1954 ( 68A Stat. 
753, 756; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a), 6106), it is 
hereby ordered that returns made in re­
spect of the taxes imposed by chapters 1, 
2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, 23, and 32, subchapters 
B, C, and D of chapter 33, and subchap­
ter B of chapter 37 of such Code shall be 
open to inspection by certain classes of 
persons and State and Federal Govern­
ment establishments in accordance and 
upon compliance with the rules and reg­
ulations prescribed by the Acting Secre­
tary of the Treasury in the Treasury 
decision relating thereto approved by me 
this date.
This order shall become effective upon 
its filing for publication in the F ederal 
R egister , and shall on that date super­
sede Executive Order No. 10738 of No­
vember 15, 1957, to the extent that such 
order is applicable to inspection by State
tax officials after the effective date of 
this order of estate and gift-tax returns 
made under the Internal Revenue Code 
of 1939 or the Internal Revenue Code of 
1954.
Dwight  D. E isenhower
T he  W hite  H ouse ,
January 17,1961.

BOARD OF INCOME TAX RETURNS

ENUE CODE OF 1954
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 6103(a) of the Internal 
Revenue Code of 1954 ( 68A Stat. 753;

Treasury decision approved by me this

returns by the Renegotiation Board.

fective upon its filing for publication 
in the F ederal R egister .

TURNS OF CORPORATIONS MADE

By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 6103(a) of the Internal 
Revenue Code of 1954 ( 68A Stat. 753; 26 
U.S.C. 6103(a)), it is hereby ordered that 
income tax returns of corporations made

cuting the powers conferred on such

mission Act of September 26, 1914 (38

accordance and upon compliance with 
the rules and regulations prescribed by 
the Acting Secretary of the Treasury in 
the Treasury decision approved by me

such returns by the Federal Trade 
Commission.

research_rationale:
EO 10738 is a one-paragraph authorization for State tax officials to inspect estate and gift tax returns. EO 10906 (effective 1961-01-18 on filing) superseded it for State-official inspection of returns made under the 1939 and 1954 Codes, and EO 10954 (effective as of 1961-01-18) narrowed that supersession to 1954-Code returns, leaving 1939-Code returns under EO 10738. Both are recorded as partial later events. The whole clause ended on the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). Searches: the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record two citation hits each for this order without a located text slice in the dossier, so they were not treated as evidence of continuation; the OFR disposition-note search lists the three chain events.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) EO 10906 and EO 10954 both name EO 10738 and supersede it only in part (1954-Code returns after EO 10954's amendment), so neither ends the clause as a whole; (2) no held source shows a statutory extinguishment of the authority earlier than 1986; (3) EO 12553 names EO 10738 by number and is the first instrument that ends the whole clause.","independent_command_check":"The Treasury regulations and decision named in the order are separate instruments that are not held in the packet. The successor Orders 10906 and 10954 create their own independent inspection commands; they do not carry the 1939-Code authority.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). Inspections already made under the order were completed acts; no continuing right or duty arising only from the order is shown by held evidence, and the statutory confidentiality rule in the Code is independent of the order.","scope_check":"One clause. Partial scope is recorded as later events: from 1961-01-18 the clause was superseded as to State-official inspection of estate and gift tax returns made under the 1954 Code and remained as to returns made under the 1939 Code until EO 12553. The inventory cannot split the single sentence into two disjoint spans, so the partial supersession is carried in later_events."}

Sec. 303. As used in regulations prescribed pursuant to section 
302 hereof, those terms of the said section 402 of title 37 of the 
United States Code which are quoted in the subsections of this section 
shall have the meaning or application stated with respect thereto:
(a) The term “entitled to receive basic pay” shall be considered 
applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they 
are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they 
are entitled to basic pay: Provided , that such term shall not be 
applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions 
which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would 
prevent him from receiving full basic pay.
(b) The term “when rations in kind are not available” shall be 
considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty at sta­
tions where it is determined, in accordance with regulations prescribed 
pursuant to section 302 hereof, that it is impracticable for subsist­
ence in kind to be furnished by the United States.
(c) The term “when permission to mess separately is granted” 
shall be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members on duty 
at stations or while sick in hospitals where a mess for subsisting 
enlisted members is available and when such enlisted members are 
authorized to subsist themselves independently. Such term shall also 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members during all 
periods of authorized leave, including periods of leave or delay while 
en route between duty stations.
(d) The term “when assigned to duty under emergency conditions 
where no messing facilities of the United States are available” shall 
be considered applicable in the case of enlisted members assigned to 
duty under conditions requiring extraordinary expenses for subsistence 
as determined in accordance with regulations prescribed pursuant to 
section 302 hereof.
(e) The term “being subsisted at the expense of the United States” 
shall be considered applicable to enlisted members who are subsisted 
in kind by the United States and to enlisted members while they are in 
a travel status and are entitled to a per-diem allowance in lieu of 
subsistence or to a mileage allowance.

is payable to enlisted members in accordance with section 305 of title

(d) The term “permanent station” shall mean the place on shore 
where a member is assigned to duty, or the home yard or the home port 
of a ship in which a member is required to perform duty, under orders 
in each case which do not in terms provide for the termination thereof; 
and any station on shore or any receiving ship where a member is as­

or reserve components of any of the uniformed services on active duty 
for training, the place where the training duty is being qierformed 
shall be deemed to be the permanent station of such members for the 
purposes of these regulations.
S ec. 402. Except as otherwise by statute heretofore or hereafter 
provided, a member shall be entitled to payment of basic allowances 
for quarters, in accordance with these regulations and any regulations 
prescribed pursuant hereto, during shell time or times as he is entitled 
to receive basic pay.
S ec. 403. Any quarters or housing facilities under the jurisdiction 
of any of the uniformed services in fact occupied without payment of 
rental charges (a) by a member and his dependents, or (b) at his 
permanent station by a member without dependents, or (c) by the 
dependents of a member on field duty or on sea duty or on duty at a 
station where adequate quarters are not available for his dependents, 
shall be deemed to have been assigned to such member as appropriate 
and adequate quarters, and no basic allowance for quarters shall 
accrue to such member under such circumstances unless the occupancy
(i) occurs while such member is in a duty or leave status incident to

in the case of members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine 
Corps, and the reserve components thereof, or by the appropriate 
Secretary in the case of members of the other uniformed services, or
(ii) occurs while such member is in a leave status not incident to a 
change of permanent station and does not exceed seven consecutive 
days at one location: Provided , That occupancy of quarters under such 
circumstances for a period in excess of such 7-day period or such other 
temporary period as may be authorized under standards prescribed 
by regulations issued by the Secretary concerned shall not result in 
a forfeiture of basic allowance for quarters for such 7-day or other 
authorized period: Provided further , That this paragraph shall not 
apply to occupancy of quarters as a guest of another member.

able for assignment at his perfnanent station to a member with de­
pendents, he may occupy quarters of the United States designated for

payment of basic allowances for quarters, if permitted or required to

No sunset or condition ends either item. This scope is item 2, the effective-as-of-1957-09-01 direction (offsets 2905-2967).

EO 10739 is a strike-and-insert or addition amendment of a pay-and-allowance regulation order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option B) its clauses continue, as amended, until the parent order ends. The 1962 title 37 recodification is disclosed as an unnamed earlier candidate that I read as restating without substantive change (Public Law 87-649 section 12). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 624-2142 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10749.txt, 23 FR 427): signed 1958-01-21; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Eastern Air Lines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, EAL Chapter; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. The held text of this order has local OCR damage (for example in the sentence on the board report and the standstill), but the heading, the parties, the section 10 authority and the thirty-day wording are legible. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 120; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10749_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10749_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_472822850c.txt) bears the cover date JULY 21, 1958 (date line at offsets 1223-1236 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1958-07-21. The report states that before the close of the hearings the President approved or ordered five 30-day extensions of the time limit stated in the Executive order, the last extension being until July 27, 1958 (report text offsets 6799-6985); its letter of transmittal is also dated July 21, 1958. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1958-08-20 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10749 appears in the table at offset 10638 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

re-enacted and amended by the Agricul­
tural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, 
as amended (7 U. S. C. 601 et seq.).
§  961.2 Secretary.  “Secretary” means 
the Secretary of Agriculture, or any of­
ficer or employee of the United States 
authorized to exercise the powers and to 
perform the duties of the Secretary of 
Agriculture.
§  961.3 Department of Agriculture.  
“Department of Agriculture” means the 
United States Department of Agriculture 
or any other Federal agency as may be 
authorized by Act of Congress, or by Ex­
ecutive order, to perform the price re­
porting functions of the United States 
Department of Agriculture.
§  961.4 Person. “Person” means any 
individual, partnership, corporation, as­
sociation, or any other business unit.
§  961.5 Philadelphia, Pennsylvania,  
milk, marketing area.  “Philadelphia, 
Pennsylvania, milk marketing area”, 
hereinafter called the “marketing area” 
means all the territory in the Common­
wealth of Pennsylvania situated within 
the following boundary line: Eeginning 
at a point in the Pennsylvania State line 
at the northern boundary of the Lower 
Makefleld township line in Bucks Coun­
ty, thence first westerly, thence southerly 
along said Lower Makefield township 
line to the Middletown township line; 
thence westerly and southerly along the 
Middletown township line to the Lower 
Southampton township line; thence 
northerly and thence westerly along the 
Lower Southampton township line to the 
Montgomery County line; thence north­
erly along the Montgomery County line
to the Trenton cut-off of the Pennsyl­
vania Railroad; thence westerly along 
said railroad to the Upper Dublin town­
ship line, thence along the southern and 
western boundaries of Upper Dublin 
township to the Whitemarsh township 
line; thence southerly along the White- 
marsh township line to the lower Merion 
township line; thence along the north­
ern boundary of lower Merion township 
to the Delawaré County line; thence 
northerly, westerly and southerly along 
the Delaware County line to the Pennsyl­
vania State line; thence ^easterly and 
northerly along the Pennsylvania State 
line to the point of beginning.
§  961.6 Cooperative association.  
“Cooperative association” means any 
cooperative marketing association of 
producers which the Secretary deter­
mines, after application by the associa­
tion:
(a) To be qualified under the provi­
sions of the Act of Congress of February 
18, 1922, as amended, known as the 
“Capper-Volstead Act”; and
(b) To have full authority in the sale 
of milk of its members and to be engaged 
in making collective sales of or market­
ing milk or its products for its members.
§  961.7 Producer milk plant.  “Pro­
ducer milk plant” means:
(a) A pasteurizing or bottling plant 
from which milk is disposed of during the 
month as Class I milk in the marketing 
area on routes (including routes oper­
ated by vendors), or through plant stores 
to retail or wholesale^utlets (except 
other producer milk plants) ; or
(b) Any other plant from which milk 
in the form of products designated as 
Class I milk (not including certified 
milk) is supplied during the month to a 
pasteurizing or bottling plant described 
in paragraph (a) of this section, any- 
part of which is allocated to Class I milk 
pursuant to §  961.47: Provided, That any 
such other plant shall not be included in 
this definition during any of the months 
of October, November, December and 
January in which shipments, any part of 
which is allocated to Class I milk, are 
made from the plant on less than 11 days 
during such month to such pasteurizing 
and bottling plant, or to a plant or plants 
supplying such pasteurizing or bottling 
plant unless such plant was a producer 
milk plant in at least four of £he pre­
ceding months of February through Sep­
tember: And provided further,  That in 
the case of a system operation in which 
the same handler operates both a pas­
teurizing and bottling plant(s) qualified 
as a producer milk plant(s) under para­
graph (a) of this section and two or more 
receiving plants qualified to ship milk to 
his pasteurizing and bottling plant(s), 
any of such qualified receiving plants as 
the handler may designate shall be con­
sidered as a unit (system) upon written 
notice to the market administrator set­
ting forth the plants to be included as 
a unit and the period during which such 
designation shall apply. Such notice 
and notice of any changes in designa­
tion, shall be furnished on or before the 
15th day of the month preceding the 
month to which the notice applies.

research_rationale:
EO 10749 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1958-07-21 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10749 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. The revocation in EO 12553 has no exception text, so it reaches the whole order."}

savings_residuals.reason: The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.
